title: Bridge and Typewriter
premise: In the winter of 1911, apprentice clockmaker Oscar Ishikawa is sent to a river town to repair the observatory's failing master clock, only for the season's first storm to close the bridge and trap him among strangers: a widowed archivist, her sharp-tongued niece, and a town hiding its role in a decades-old land swindle now being rewritten by the railroad's hired historians. As the clock's mechanism reveals timestamps that contradict the official record, Oscar and his unlikely found family race to document the truth before the ice breaks, the bridge reopens, and the victors' version becomes permanent. The book ends with the testimony sealed and published just as the river thaws — Oscar chooses to stay, taking over the clockworks and, at last, belonging somewhere history actually happened.
about_author: Orsen Yarrow is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent years restoring mechanical instruments in small-town collections across the northern river valleys. They write historical fiction about the people history overlooks, one repaired object at a time.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Oscar Ishikawa, POV. A letter arrives at the workshop summoning him to repair the observatory master clock at Verlow's Landing. His master dismisses it as small work; Oscar privately hopes the journey will make him someone things happen to. Emotional beat: restless yearning disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Crossing Over
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. He rides the last coach across the iron bridge as snow begins, glimpsing the town's shuttered mills and the observatory on its hill. A girl on the coach warns him not to ask about the year the records burned. Emotional beat: ominous arrival, first hint of buried history.

chapters.title: The Master Clock
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. In the observatory he meets keeper Ada Verlow, who shows him the great clock — and a locked drawer of ledgers she says are 'not his concern.' He begins diagnosing the escapement. Emotional beat: professional wonder shadowed by secrecy.

chapters.title: Bridge Closed
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The storm closes the bridge; the ferry is iced in. Stranded until thaw, Oscar takes a room above the archive where Ada lives with her niece, Juniper. Emotional beat: frustration curdling into reluctant curiosity about the town.

chapters.title: Juniper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Sharp and suspicious of the outsider, Juniper catalogs the archive alone, revealing to the reader fragments of the 1880s land grants — signatures that don't match. She hides a page from both Ada and Oscar. Emotional beat: guarded complicity.

chapters.title: Teeth of the Escapement
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Repairing the clock, Oscar finds a worn cam added decades after construction — the clock was altered to run minutes fast during specific seasons. Someone used it to falsify timestamps. Emotional beat: dawning alarm.

chapters.title: The Railroad Men
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Two historians employed by the Northern Pacific arrive ahead of the thaw, ostensibly to 'preserve' town records. Their courtesy has teeth. Ada welcomes them; Oscar watches her hands shake. Emotional beat: menace beneath politeness.

chapters.title: What the River Took
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada recalls the flood of '89 that drowned the original grant office — and her husband, who died gathering documents against the railroad. She has spent years afraid rather than fighting. Emotional beat: grief confessed, resolve kindled.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Strangers
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar confronts Ada with the altered cam; she finally opens the locked drawer. The three form an uneasy pact: verify the ledgers against the clock's own maintenance logs before the historians finish their 'inventory.' Emotional beat: found family coalescing.

chapters.title: The Millwright's Daughter
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Juniper tracks down elderly Mrs. Halloway, daughter of the millwright whose signature was forged, and records her testimony on wax cylinders. First living witness secured. Emotional beat: fragile triumph.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The railroad men begin cataloging the archive, box by box, getting closer to the grant ledgers. Oscar must repair the master clock under their watching eyes while hiding what it proves. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension.

chapters.title: A Broken Escapement
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Sabotage: the clock's escapement is deliberately damaged overnight, destroying evidence of the alteration. Oscar suspects the younger historian saw him measuring the cam. Emotional beat: betrayal and fear.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. With the clock stopped, time itself seems to stop; Ada nearly surrenders, ready to let the past stay drowned. Juniper reads her father's unsent letters aloud. Emotional beat: despair turning toward courage.

chapters.title: Rebuilding Time
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar hand-cuts a new escape wheel from memory, working three days straight while Juniper distracts the historians and Ada forges their access passes to the county records office. Emotional beat: obsessive hope.

chapters.title: The County Vault
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Using the forged pass, Juniper reaches the county vault and photographs the true grant ledger — but the elder historian follows her, and she barely escapes across the frozen millrace. Emotional beat: terror and defiance.

chapters.title: Ice Cracking
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The river groans; thaw is early this year. The clock runs again, its corrected time matching the photographed ledger exactly. But the historians have wired ahead: a company lawyer arrives on the first ferry. Emotional beat: countdown pressure.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Offer
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The lawyer offers Ada money and her husband's restored good name if she surrenders the ledgers as 'damaged and unreliable.' She refuses, quoting her husband's own words back at him. Emotional beat: moral climax of conscience.

chapters.title: Sealing the Record
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The trio compiles everything — cylinders, photographs, the cam itself — into a sworn deposition witnessed by half the town in the observatory under the running master clock, every timestamp now honest. Emotional beat: communal catharsis.

chapters.title: The Historian's Choice
chapters.summary: Elder historian Marsh, POV (brief shift). Confronted with the evidence, Marsh — once an honest scholar — signs as witness rather than suppress it, damning his employer. Emotional beat: redemption of a compromised man.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The ice breaks; the bridge reopens. The lawyer leaves empty-handed; the deposition goes out on the morning coach to the state press. Oscar stands on the bridge he arrived on, no longer needing it as an exit. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Apprentice No More
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Ada offers him the observatory keeper's position; Juniper offers him a place at their table without irony for the first time. He wires his old master that he isn't coming back. Emotional beat: chosen belonging.

chapters.title: Keeping Time
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV, one year later. The town's land titles are restored; the clock keeps true time; Juniper's oral histories hang framed beside the pendulum. Oscar winds the mechanism each dawn, part of a history that finally happened to him. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
